content.introduction: The United States economic indicators for September 2026 show an increase in the Coincident Economic Index® (CEI) by 0.3% to 115.3 (2016=100), with a 0.9% rise over the six months between March and September 2026. The industrial production mom was up 0.7% in September 2026, and the unemployment rate was 4.2% in September 2026. The GDP annual growth rate was 2.2% in June 2026. The durable goods orders were up 0% in August 2026, and the stock market points were at 7649 in October 2026. The sources do not provide a definitive answer for some specific indicators like federal government payrolls and financial activities payrolls.

The Conference Board Coincident Economic Index® (CEI) for the US increased by 0.3% in September 2026 to 115.3 (2016=100), following a 0.1% increase in August. Overall, the CEI rose by 0.9% over the six months between March and September 2026, up from its 0.2% growth over the previous six months.  The composite economic indexes are key elements in an analytic system designed to signal peaks and troughs in the business cycle. Comprised of multiple independent indicators, the indexes are constructed to summarize and reveal common turning points in the economy in a clearer and more convincing manner than any individual component. The U.S. Census Bureau’s economic indicator surveys provide monthly and quarterly data that are timely, reliable, and offer comprehensive measures of the U.S. economy. These surveys provide a variety of statistics covering construction, housing, international trade, retail trade, wholesale trade, services and manufacturing.
